insights.headline: Out of 83 posts describing a pull-back, 27 cite lost trust in the platform while 2 cite market falls.
insights.so_what: This suggests investigating whether platform trust issues play a larger role in decisions to stop payments than market drops. Examining what triggers this loss of trust could clarify why posts describe stopping payments.
insights.caveat: The findings are limited to reasons explicitly mentioned in 83 sample posts.

insights.headline: Confidence is expressed in 73 posts about continuing, whereas anger is expressed in 66 posts about pulling back.
insights.so_what: This suggests investigating how negative experiences turn feeling confident into feeling angry. Tracking this emotional change may highlight why posts describe stopping payments.
insights.caveat: Only 9 continuing posts and 5 pull-back posts state how frequently the poster checks investments.

insights.headline: Failed instalments account for 29 percent of the 117 total lapse posts in the sample.
insights.so_what: This suggests investigating technical or banking interruptions that prevent planned contributions. Understanding these unchosen failures could explain why payments stop without action by the poster.
insights.caveat: The counts rely entirely on post text rather than transaction error logs.

insights.headline: Of 473 extracted posts, 26% say how long the person has invested, 0% their income type and 23% whether they are first-time investors.
insights.so_what: Segment and stage questions (who drops off, and when) mostly cannot be answered from public posts; they need the app's own data or primary research.
insights.caveat: Absence from posts does not mean absence in the population; people rarely write these details down.
